title: Monetary Policy Report—October 2024
summary: The Bank of Canada reduced its target for the overnight rate by 50 basis points to 3¾% amid inflation now around the 2% target. The Canadian economy remains in excess supply with a softened labour market, while Canada's economic growth is projected to average 2¼% over 2025 and 2026 as lower interest rates support consumer spending and business investment.
key_points: Bank of Canada cut policy rate by 50 bps to 3¾% (Bank Rate at 4%, deposit rate at 3¾%)
CPI inflation has fallen to around 2%, within the Bank's control range of 1% to 3%
Canadian economy continues to be in excess supply; labour market softening with unemployment concentrated among newcomers and youth
Canada GDP growth projected to average 2¼% over 2025 and 2026, driven by consumer spending and business investment
Global economy expected to grow at around 3%; US growth strong but slowing, euro area subdued, China weakened by property crisis
Wage growth remains elevated relative to productivity, creating ongoing inflationary pressure
why_it_matters: This Bank of Canada Monetary Policy Report signals the beginning of an easing cycle with a 50 bps cut, indicating the central bank views inflation as sufficiently contained to shift focus toward supporting growth. The report provides Canada's official economic projections, which are critical for CAD market participants and those with Canadian dollar exposures. The balance between excess supply, softening labour markets, and above-productivity wage growth creates a complex backdrop for future policy decisions.
macro_context: The Bank of Canada is executing its first rate cut cycle as inflation has returned to target. The report projects Canada's economy emerging from excess supply conditions with 2.25% average growth through 2025-2026. Global headwinds include China's property crisis weighing on oil demand, while the US shows resilience but expected slowing. This easing path contrasts with the prior tightening cycle, establishing a new rate trajectory for CAD markets.
